promise_quote: Complete the Mu2 e and muon g-2 projects.
science_question: Search for the charged-lepton-flavor-violating conversion of a muon to an electron in the field of a nucleus at unprecedented sensitivity.
rationale: Table 1 row 'Muon program: Mu2e, Muon g-2' lists Mu2e and Muon g-2 together; split into separate bets since each is a distinct named experiment with its own Snowmass description. Scenario A cell carries the table footnote 'Mu2e small reprofile needed'; Scenario C cell was not distinguishable from the extracted table text (only two Y-groups visible for A/B) so C is inferred as continuing (Y) based on Recommendation 22's unconditional 'complete' language and Figure 1 showing Mu2e as an ongoing large project. Hosted at Fermilab (a DOE national laboratory).

promise_quote: Complete the Mu2 e and muon g-2 projects.
science_question: Measure the muon's anomalous magnetic moment (g-2) with improved precision to test for a discrepancy with the Standard Model prediction.
rationale: Same Table 1 row as Mu2e ('Muon program: Mu2e, Muon g-2'); see Mu2e entry for notes on Scenario C ambiguity. Text (p.44) notes the existing measured g-2 value differs from the Standard Model prediction by 3.5 standard deviations, which this experiment aims to sharpen. Fermilab-hosted, DOE.

promise_quote: The HL-LHC is strongly supported and is the first high-priority large-category project in our recommended program.
science_question: Measure Higgs boson couplings to a few-percent precision and extend the search for new particles and dark matter production to higher luminosity and mass reach using the high-luminosity LHC.
rationale: Encompasses the accelerator upgrade and both ATLAS and CMS experiments (Recommendation 10). International project hosted at CERN with major US construction/operation roles; agency is the US portion funded jointly by DOE-HEP and NSF Physics per p.10 text ('successful interagency partnership'). Target date from 'The HL-LHC will operate in the 2020s' (p.27).

promise_quote: The ongoing Phase-1 upgrade should be completed by 2018.
science_question: Maintain and prepare LHC/ATLAS/CMS performance ahead of the luminosity upgrade to continue Higgs, dark matter, and new-particle searches at 14 TeV.
rationale: Not its own Table 1 row; appears only in the Figure 1 timeline, whose caption explicitly states 'The LHC: Phase 1 upgrade is a Medium project, but shown next to the HL-LHC for context.' Same US interagency (DOE+NSF) funding context as HL-LHC/LHC program.

promise_quote: Form a new international collaboration to design and execute a highly capable Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility (LBNF) hosted by the U.S. To proceed, a project plan and identified resources must exist to meet the minimum requirements in the text. LBNF is the highest-priority large project in its timeframe.
science_question: Measure CP violation in neutrino oscillations and determine the neutrino mass hierarchy using a high-intensity wideband beam and a large underground liquid-argon detector, with sensitivity to proton decay and supernova neutrinos.
rationale: Table 1 combines LBNF and PIP-II in one row ('LBNF + PIP-II'); split here since Recommendations 13 and 14 treat them separately. Scenario A cell carries footnote 'LBNF components delayed relative to Scenario B'; Scenario B cell reads 'Y, enhanced'; the extracted table text shows no distinct Scenario C token for this row, so C='Y' is inferred (LBNF continues as highest-priority project; Scenario C's distinct addition is a separate large water-Cherenkov detector, tracked as its own bet). Intended to be internationally funded, hosted by Fermilab (DOE). Target date range: construction phase begins 'around 2018' (p.12); minimum exposure goal 'by the 2035 timeframe' (p.11-12). Driver: neutrino-mass primary; also addresses the Unknown driver via proton-decay/baryon-number-violation searches (p.44).

promise_quote: Upgrade the Fermilab proton accelerator complex to produce higher intensity beams. R&D for the Proton Improvement Plan II (PIP-II) should proceed immediately, followed by construction, to provide proton beams of >1 MW by the time of first operation of the new long-baseline neutrino facility.
science_question: Provide a proton beam of greater than 1 MW power from the upgraded Fermilab accelerator complex to enable LBNF's wideband neutrino beam and other high-intensity physics.
rationale: Shares the combined 'LBNF + PIP-II' Table 1 row with LBNF; see LBNF entry for the same Scenario-C cell ambiguity. Redirects former Project-X activities and some existing GARD accelerator R&D funding (p.9, p.15-16). Fermilab/DOE.

promise_quote: As the physics case is extremely strong, we plan in all Scenarios for ILC support at some level through a decision point within the next five years.
science_question: Measure Higgs boson couplings to Standard Model particles and to the dark sector to the percent or sub-percent level, in a model-independent way, using clean e+e- collisions.
rationale: Table 1 extraction shows 'R&D only' (Scenario A) and 'R&D, Y' immediately followed by driver checkmarks with no clearly separated Scenario C token; Scenario C='Y' is inferred from the Executive Summary statement of 'a high-priority option in Scenario C to enable the U.S. to play world-leading roles' (p. vii) and text (p.11) noting 'some hardware contributions may be possible in Scenario B.' Agency not explicitly named in the report for ILC R&D funding (drawn from general DOE-HEP/NSF-PHY research program, per p.11 discussion of US design leadership, but not stated as such). Target date 2019 reflects the stated 'decision point within the next 5 years' from the report's 2014 publication, not a construction/operation date.

promise_quote: the high cost makes it impossible to pursue at the same time as PIP-II and LBNF, which are the primary objectives.
science_question: Provide a precisely known-flux source of ~GeV neutrinos and antineutrinos via a muon storage ring, for sensitive sterile-neutrino searches and precision cross-section measurements.
rationale: Table 1 places NuSTORM under 'Large Projects' with N/N/N across all scenarios (declined); text (p.32) explicitly calls NuSTORM 'large-scale,' confirming the size class. Fermilab-based concept, DOE.

promise_quote: A strategy focusing resources on moving ahead as fast as possible on LBNF is therefore favored.
science_question: Build a liquid argon TPC at the Ash River site on the existing NuMI beamline to improve knowledge of oscillation parameters and offset R&D costs for LBNF.
rationale: Table 1 places RADAR under 'Large Projects' with N/N/N across all scenarios, despite its description reading as a smaller-scale concept than the other Large Projects; size_class follows the report's own table placement per extraction rules. Ash River site is part of Fermilab's NOvA infrastructure, DOE.

promise_quote: Complete LSST as planned.
science_question: Measure the positions, shapes, and distances of billions of galaxies and hundreds of thousands of clusters and Type Ia supernovae to constrain dark energy and structure growth to percent-level precision.
rationale: Text (p.14) calls LSST 'a good example of successful multi-agency cooperation'; agency inferred as DOE+NSF given the report frames US particle-physics funding as exactly these two agencies (DOE-HEP, NSF-PHY) throughout. Driver checkmarks in Table 1 align with Neutrinos and Cosm. Accel. columns (not Dark Matter), consistent with text (p.4-5) crediting LSST's structure measurements for both dark-energy/inflation and neutrino-mass constraints. Target date is inferred from the Cosmic Acceleration Driver's 'Goals and Timeframes' bullets (p.39: structure measured to 10% by 2020, percent precision by 2030), which are not explicitly tied to LSST by name in that sentence, so this attribution is an interpretation rather than a direct project-dated quote.

promise_quote: Proceed immediately with a broad second-generation (G2) dark matter direct detection program with capabilities described in the text. Invest in this program at a level significantly above that called for in the 2012 joint agency announcement of opportunity.
science_question: Search for WIMP-nucleon (and axion) dark matter interactions across a broad mass range (1 GeV to 100 TeV) with at least an order-of-magnitude improvement in cross-section sensitivity over current experiments.
rationale: Agency inferred as DOE+NSF from 'the 2012 joint agency announcement of opportunity' referenced in the recommendation text. Target date taken from the Dark Matter Driver's 'Goals and Timeframes' bullet (p.37): 'Probe dark matter interactions with ordinary matter over a range of dark matter masses and interaction types, with large and important discovery reach (2015-2024)' -- this maps to the G2 program by context but does not name 'DM G2' explicitly in that sentence.

promise_quote: Support one or more third-generation (G3) direct detection experiments, guided by the results of the preceding searches. Seek a globally complementary program and increased international partnership in G3 experiments.
science_question: Extend dark-matter direct-detection sensitivity down to the neutrino-background coherent-scattering limit, guided by G2 results, via one or more US-led third-generation experiments.
rationale: Size_class (medium) inferred from Table 1 section placement (no explicit 'medium'/'mid-scale' quote found for DM G3 specifically, unlike ORKA/LAr1/CMB-S4). Scenario A cell reads 'Y, reduced'; Executive Summary confirms 'third-generation direct detection dark matter capabilities would be reduced or delayed' under Scenario A. Target date inferred from Dark Matter Driver goals bullet (p.37): 'measure the dark matter particle mass and all properties... Otherwise, continue to probe lower cross sections down to the background limits due to neutrino-nucleon coherent scattering (2021-2030)', which follows the G2 bullet in sequence but does not name G3 explicitly.

promise_quote: Support CMB experiments as part of the core particle physics program. The multidisciplinary nature of the science warrants continued multiagency support.
science_question: Measure the amplitude of inflationary gravitational waves imprinted in the cosmic microwave background to percent-level precision, and constrain the sum of neutrino masses.
rationale: Text explicitly states the size class: 'As the scale of CMB experiments grows from Stage 3, which is of the size of an experiment in the small project portfolio, to Stage 4 (S4), which is mid-scale' (p.14). Target date taken from the Cosmic Acceleration Driver goals bullet (p.39): '...either measure the amplitude of this signal to the percent level or constrain the spectrum to sub-percent accuracy to distinguish between models of inflation (2025)', which describes CMB-S4's inflation measurement but does not name it in that exact clause.

rank_or_scenario: A:Further development of concept encouraged|B:Further development of concept encouraged|C:Further development of concept encouraged
promise_quote: PINGU could play a very important role as part of a larger upgrade of IceCube, or as a separate upgrade, but more work is required.
science_question: Determine the neutrino mass hierarchy using a large sample of atmospheric neutrinos, and probe low-mass (down to ~5 GeV) WIMP dark matter, via an infill array at the IceCube facility.
rationale: Table 1's Scenario A/B/C cells for PINGU appear to be a single merged cell spanning all three scenarios ('Further development of concept encouraged'), rather than three distinct Y/N values, so the same text is repeated for A, B, and C; this reading is an interpretation of the extracted table layout, not a clean three-column parse. Size class (medium) is inferred from table section placement, not an explicit textual statement. Agency not stated in the report (IceCube/PINGU host facility is not named with a funding agency in the text).

promise_quote: Unfortunately, due to resource constraints and anticipated conflicts with the highest priority items in the Fermilab program, P5 cannot recommend moving ahead with ORKA at this time.
science_question: Measure the rare kaon decay K+ -> pi+ nu nu-bar with improved sensitivity, exploiting the Standard Model's clean theoretical prediction to search for multi-TeV-scale new physics.
rationale: Text explicitly calls ORKA 'this mid-size project' (p.15), confirming Medium size class independent of table-section placement. Fermilab experiment, DOE.

promise_quote: CHIPS proposes a large water Cherenkov detector in a water-filled mine pit, first at a NuMI off-axis location, and possibly later as an off-axis LBNF detector.
science_question: Use a water Cherenkov detector deployed in a flooded mine pit on the NuMI off-axis beamline to gain incremental sensitivity to neutrino mass hierarchy and CP violation beyond NOvA/T2K.
rationale: Size class (medium) inferred from Table 1 section placement, not an explicit textual size statement for CHIPS specifically. Decline is evidenced by Table 1's N/N/N and the surrounding text favoring LBNF over RADAR/CHIPS ('A strategy focusing resources on moving ahead as fast as possible on LBNF is therefore favored', p.13), rather than a CHIPS-specific decline sentence. NuMI beamline is part of Fermilab, DOE.

promise_quote: LAr1 is a mid-scale short-baseline accelerator-based experiment to address both the neutrino and antineutrino SBL anomalies. An appropriate combination of smaller near-term projects may accomplish most of these goals at much lower cost, so proceeding with LAr1 is not recommended at this time.
science_question: Address the short-baseline neutrino and antineutrino oscillation anomalies with a mid-scale liquid-argon detector.
rationale: Text explicitly calls LAr1 'mid-scale' (p.13, and again p.32: 'LAr1 and NuSTORM are mid-scale and large-scale, respectively'), confirming Medium size class, and explicitly states it is 'not recommended at this time.' Fermilab-based, DOE.

promise_quote: Build DESI as a major step forward in dark energy science, if funding permits (see Scenarios discussion below).
science_question: Measure the expansion history of the Universe via baryon acoustic oscillation distances to 25 million galaxies and quasars, constraining dark energy parameters to the percent level over ten billion years.
source_locator: p. 17, Table 1 (Additional Small Projects); p. 13, Recommendation 16
rationale: Table 1 explicitly lists DESI under the 'Additional Small Projects' heading, confirming Small size class; interagency (DOE + NSF, via use of the NSF-operated Mayall telescope on Kitt Peak, p.13) use noted in text as 'an interagency opportunity for the use of the Mayall 4-meter facility.' Target date inferred from the Cosmic Acceleration Driver goals bullet (p.39): 'Measure the parameters that characterize dark energy to 5% precision (2020) and then improve to 1% (2025)', which is DESI's stated capability elsewhere in the text (p.40) but not explicitly dated to DESI in that exact sentence.

promise_quote: Invest in CTA as part of the small projects portfolio if the critical NSF Astronomy funding can be obtained.
science_question: Search for dark matter annihilation signals in the inner Galaxy and dwarf spheroidal galaxies via ground-based gamma-ray astronomy, reaching the WIMP thermal annihilation cross section for masses up to ~10 TeV.
rationale: Not its own Table 1 row (folded into the small projects portfolio conceptually); recommendation is conditional on NSF Astronomy funding, which the report itself notes goes beyond the two named HEP agencies -- 'the project costs should be shared by NSF Astronomy, NSF Physics, and DOE' (p.14); rendered here as DOE+NSF since NSF Astronomy falls outside the allowed DOE/NSF/DOE+NSF/not-stated value set, noted here rather than invented as a new value.

promise_quote: Host a large water Cherenkov neutrino detector to complement the LBNF large liquid argon detector, unifying the global long-baseline neutrino community to take full advantage of the world's highest intensity neutrino beam at Fermilab.
science_question: Complement LBNF's liquid argon far detector with a large water Cherenkov detector at an optimized site to unify the global long-baseline neutrino community around Fermilab's beam.
source_locator: p. vii, Executive Summary; p. 19, Section 2.3 (Scenario C)
rationale: One of three Scenario C (unconstrained budget) high-priority items; the report does not give this detector its own proper name (unlike CHIPS, a different, smaller, near-surface water Cherenkov concept that was explicitly declined elsewhere), so 'Water Cherenkov Detector' is a descriptive short name rather than the report's own label. Not in Table 1. Only recommended under Scenario C.

promise_quote: Redirect former Project-X activities and some existing accelerator R&D to improvements of the Fermilab accelerator complex that will provide proton beams with power greater than one megawatt by the time of first operation of the new long-baseline neutrino facility.
science_question: (As originally conceived) provide a multi-megawatt proton source at Fermilab to support a broad program of neutrino and rare-process precision experiments.
rationale: Project-X as originally proposed is superseded/redirected into PIP-II and the reformulated Fermilab accelerator complex plan; treated as a declined bet distinct from PIP-II, which is the report's new recommended project. Fermilab, DOE.

promise_quote: These minimum requirements are not met by the current LBNE project's CD-1 minimum scope.
science_question: (As the CD-1 minimum-scope design) measure long-baseline neutrino oscillations with a domestically funded beam and a small, surface-sited far detector.
rationale: LBNE is the pre-2014 predecessor project to LBNF; the report describes its CD-1 minimum-scope configuration as inadequate and calls for a change in approach, reformulating it into the internationally funded LBNF. The decline is evidenced through this contextual passage and the surrounding restructuring narrative rather than a single explicit 'not recommended' sentence naming LBNE.

promise_quote: Reassess the Muon Accelerator Program (MAP). Incorporate into the GARD program the MAP activities that are of general importance to accelerator R&D, and consult with international partners on the early termination of MICE.
science_question: Demonstrate ionization cooling of a muon beam, a key enabling technology for a future muon collider or neutrino factory.
rationale: MICE (Muon Ionization Cooling Experiment) is hosted at the Rutherford Appleton Laboratory (UK), described in Section 3.6 as part of the US Muon Accelerator Program (MAP); MAP itself is excluded from this list as an R&D program, but MICE is a specific named facility that the report explicitly recommends terminating early, in consultation with international partners. Not its own Table 1 row (only MAP appears there, with N/N/N).
